questions.q: In plain words, what is a data lakehouse?
options: A second warehouse that keeps a full copy of your data
Open files in cheap cloud storage, plus a layer that adds warehouse features
A tool that cleans and fixes your data for you
A new file format that only one vendor supports
questions.explain: That is the whole idea. Cheap, open files at the bottom, and a layer on top that brings warehouse features such as all-or-nothing changes.

questions.q: Why did companies start looking for something better than running a lake and a warehouse side by side?
options: Data was stored twice, and copies between the two went stale
Cloud storage became too cheap to be useful
Warehouses stopped being able to run reports
Lakes could not hold any files at all
questions.explain: The paper names reliability, stale data, weak machine learning support and the higher cost of storing data twice. The lakehouse answer is to keep one copy that all tools query.

questions.q: Two people change and read the same table at the same moment. What does the table layer do for them?
options: It makes sure the readers see a change fully or not at all, never half done
It locks everyone out until one person finishes
It makes every query run much faster
It stores the raw files in the cloud
questions.explain: The table layer tracks which files make up the table, so a change either fully happens or does not happen at all. A report that started earlier keeps using the version it loaded.

questions.q: Is a lakehouse the same thing as Delta Lake, Iceberg or Hudi?
options: Yes, Delta Lake is the lakehouse
Yes, but only Iceberg counts
No, they are cloud storage services
No, the lakehouse is the general idea, and those are ways to build the table layer
questions.explain: AWS, IBM and Databricks all describe a lakehouse as an architecture. Delta Lake, Iceberg and Hudi are the table formats named as ways to build it.

questions.q: Which of these does a lakehouse NOT do for you?
options: Keep data as open files in cheap storage
Let different tools read the same tables
Write your data cleaning logic and look after the tables
Show readers a change all at once, not half done
questions.explain: Sadly, the housework stays with you. The paper says you still write the cleaning logic, though with fewer steps, and tables need regular upkeep.
